title: More than Half of People in Japan Use AI
paragraphs: From answering questions to writing emails and helping with everyday tasks, generative AI is becoming part of day-to-day life for more people in Japan.
A new survey by the Nippon Research Center found that 56% of people aged 20 to 69 had used generative AI as of June 2026.
And for the first time, just over half of those who were surveyed said they were currently using the technology.
And it's not just young people who are using AI more.
People in their 20s were still the most likely to have tried it, at 68%, followed by those in their 30s at 61% and those in their 40s at 58%.
But older generations are catching up. Among people in their 50s, 55% had used generative AI, while 45% of those in their 60s had tried it. In March 2025, both groups were still at around 20%.
So which AI tools are people in Japan using?
ChatGPT was the most popular, with 30% of people saying they currently use it. Google's Gemini was close behind at 29%, followed by Microsoft's Copilot at 15%.
The survey also looked at what people were using these tools for.

Finding information and doing research was the most common reason, mentioned by around 60% of current AI users. Another 30% used AI to come up with ideas, while about a quarter used it to write or check emails and documents.
Interestingly, the share of people using AI for research has been growing, while the share using it to generate ideas has fallen.
